alex: heads up — after the fp8 microkernel rollout to canary, we see a p95/p99 regression on long-seq workloads. digging in now, but numbers are ~12% p95 and ~18% p99 higher for redwood-1b/seq2048 under continuous batching

alex: quick summary from yesterday's smoke: throughput is fine, latency tail jumps on mixed small shapes (many seq < 256 + some 2048). lots of padding waste and repeated KV cache flushes on the same requests.

rachel: timeline? was this after the kernel selector change (auto-fp8-fallback)? @kevin any rollout notes?

alex: yes, rolled auto-fp8-fallback -> enabled fast fp8 kernels for eligible layers. selector logs show we pick fp8_gemm_128x64 for many layers but then fall back to int8_gemm_64x64 for others mid-inference. that flip seems correlated with cache churn.

kevin: can you paste the perf trace and kernel selection log snip?

alex: pasted below (bench run trimmed):
```
$ bench/trace --model redwood-1b --seq 2048 --batch 8 --continuous
[trace] batch shapes: [8x2048], [12x128], [4x64], ... (continuous pack)
[kernel] layer 20: selected fp8_gemm_128x64 (accel=1.23x)
[kernel] layer 21: fallback -> int8_gemm_64x64 (accel=0.9x)
[cache] kv: mem-mapped hits=92% evictions=8% (thrash pattern)
[latency] p50=48ms p95=134ms p99=298ms
[pad] padding_waste=27% (most from small shapes padded to 128)
```

sam: ugh, that 27% padding waste + kernel switching cost could explain the tail. continuous batching combined lots of tiny requests with a few huge seqs — kernel shapes are mismatched.

rachel: two hypotheses: 1) fp8 microkernels have stricter tile shape constraints so we end up with more pad. 2) calibration/scales for fp8 are causing occasional numeric corrections that trigger slower code paths.

oliver: i noticed per-layer quant scale recompute in the fp8 path when KV tensors hit certain ranges -> this causes a sync and falls back to a safer kernel. could be the calibration not covering the long-seq distribution.

kevin: tests to run:
- rerun bench with `--batching-mode=shape-preserving` to avoid mixing tiny+huge
- try forcing int8 for layers with kv_size < threshold `--force-kernel=int8:kv<256`
- run offline fp8 calibration using long-seq traces and re-upload scales

alex: i ran shape-preserving already — tail improves ~9% but overall token/sec drops a bit (lost packing efficiency). forcing int8 on small-kv layers restored p99 to baseline but dropped p50 a little.

perf-bot: regression alert: canary redwood-1b fp8-rollout -> p99 +18% (compare: baseline 252ms -> canary 298ms). link: https://perf.internal/runs/1754123000

sam: what about making the kernel selector padding-aware? prefer kernels that minimize pad-waste even if microkernel nominal throughput is slightly lower.

kevin: agree. we can add a cost model: effective_throughput = kernel_peak * (1 - padding_waste) - kernel_switch_penalty. choose argmax. need data for kernel_switch_penalty (measured in ms).

alex: added a simple script to estimate switch penalty:
```
# rough numbers from local traces
fp8->int8 switch penalty ~= 2.8ms per occurrence
int8->fp8 switch penalty ~= 3.1ms (locks + scale recompute)
```

oliver: also think about KV cache layout: if we change KV layout to align with fp8 tile boundaries we can reduce recompute. small change: pack KV rows into 128-wide buckets for fp8 kernels. covers many small shapes without pad.

rachel: tradeoffs? memory overhead?

oliver: adds ~6% transient buffer overhead for common configs. but reduces padding by ~15% in our sim.

kevin: longer term: improve calibration pipeline to generate per-shard fp8 scales from a more representative sample (long-seq heavy). short term: revert auto-fp8 for continuous batching or add routing rule: if continuous batch mixes seq<256 with >1024, prefer int8 route.

alex: propose immediate mitigations:
- add routing rule for mixed-shape continuous batches -> int8 (canary)
- implement padding-aware cost model in kernel selector (low risk)
- run extended calibration on long-seq traces this week

sam: +1 to that plan. also add a perf test that simulates continuous mixed workload with KV churn (daily job).

rachel: i'll open a ticket with tasks and owners. @kevin take kernel selector, @oliver take kv layout, @alex own canary rule + perf job.

kevin: on it. will prototype cost model and measure decision latency before enabling.

ops-bot: deploy canary rule to canary-cluster-3 scheduled in 15m.

alex: thanks. i'll monitor perf dashboards and post updates. any objections to delaying full fp8 rollout until we validate these? :thumbsup: / :thumbsdown:

kevin: :thumbsup:

sam: :thumbsup:

oliver: :thumbsup:

rachel: closing loop — good catch alex.
